reasoning: Split-open corn stalk showing shredded pith with only vascular strands remaining, covered with numerous tiny dark specks (microsclerotia) giving a granular appearance. This is the hallmark of charcoal stalk rot caused by Macrophomina phaseolina. Distinguished from Anthracnose stalk rot (which shows shiny black rind discoloration) and Diplodia stalk rot (which shows small black pycnidia on lower internodes rather than scattered microsclerotia on shredded pith).
